aiVerification.summary: The draft incorrectly merges two separate tests and assigns the dry-time comparison to the wrong baseline, so it is not safe as final evidence.
issues: Changed factor is incorrectly defined as 'Normal of C2 vs Use VP + CD change dry time 3s -> 4s', mixing Test 1 VP/CD lot transfer evidence with Test 2 dry-time evidence.
Baseline condition for Test 2 should be Normal dry time 3s, not Normal of C2.

Test 1 contains at least two separate comparisons: E2 using VP+CD of C2 vs Normal E2, and likely C2 using VP+CD of E2 vs Normal C2; the draft only captures Normal of C2 and omits the matching changed C2 condition row.
Outcome grouping is incomplete because each outcome contains only one side of the comparison rather than paired baseline and changed conditions.
Evidence for Test 2 omits the baseline row Function!32 from the changed factor evidence and cites Function!31 without showing it in contextRows.
The draft uses Function!22 Normal of C2 as evidence for a dry-time changed factor, which is not supported by the cited context.
correctionPlan: Split the workbook into separate changed-factor contexts or separate review cases for Test 1 VP/CD lot transfer and Test 2 dry-time change.
For Test 1, pair E2 Use VP+CD of C2 with Normal E2, and pair C2 Use VP+CD of E2 with Normal C2 if the missing changed-condition row is present in the source.
For Test 2, define the changed factor as UC1/sub 1 VP+CD dry time changed from 3s to 4s, with baseline Normal dry time 3s and changed condition dry time 4s.
Include both baseline and changed-condition rows in each outcome's comparisonRows and subResults.
Re-extract or cite the missing table rows around Function!19-22 and Function!31-32 so all paired values are visible and verifiable.
Update evidenceRows to include the title/problem rows, test description rows, and all directly relevant result rows for each comparison.
aiVerification.evidencePolicy: Current row citations are not sufficient because they omit required paired baseline/test rows and support an incorrect changed-factor grouping.
